title: kdeplasma-addons applets/comic with multi-screen pops up the full-size comic on the wrong screen
line: With several screens, the Comic widget's full-size comic now opens centred on the screen the widget is on instead of the first screen.
explanation: ComicApplet::positionFullView() centred the full-size comic window on window->screen(). That PlasmaCore.Dialog has no visual or transient parent, so its screen is just Qt's default (the first screen), not the screen of the widget that opened it, and with several screens the comic landed on whichever screen came first. The window is now centred on the available area of the applet's containment's screen (Corona::availableScreenRect), falling back to the old behaviour when the containment has no screen.

commits.message:
applets/comic: open the full-size comic on the widget's screen

The full-size comic window has no transient parent, so its screen was
the default first screen and it always opened centred there, whatever
screen the widget is on. Centre it on the applet's own screen instead.

BUG: 504829

media.caption: Two outputs, Comic widget on the right one: middle-click opens the full-size comic centred on the left output (sweep tester's shot, same master build)
With the fix, middle-click on the same widget opens the full-size comic centred on the right output
The zoom button in the widget's button bar also opens it on the right output
A second Comic widget on the left output (with the panel) still opens it there, centred in the area above the panel

reviews.text: Clean fix in ComicApplet::positionFullView() that centers the parentless full-size comic dialog on the applet containment's screen via Corona::availableScreenRect() instead of the dialog's default first screen. It handles missing containment/corona/screen safely by falling back to window->screen()->availableGeometry(), and avoids covering panels on the target screen. Multi-screen verification across both outputs and both trigger paths (middle-click and zoom button) confirms the fix.

The diagnosis is right: the parentless PlasmaCore.Dialog's screen() is Qt's default screen, so positionFullView centred it on whichever output came first. Centring on Corona::availableScreenRect of the applet's containment screen puts it where the reporter expects, keeps the old fallback when there is no screen, and avoids the panel area. The before/after shots on two outputs plus the zoom-button and left-output checks prove it, and the duplicate 510812 is the same path. Minor nitpick: the dialog's QWindow::screen() still starts on the first output, so on mixed-scale setups the first frame may use the wrong scale until Wayland's enter event; calling setScreen() on the target QScreen would make that airtight. That case is untested, as the notes say.
